podcast.title: Considered "Too Light" for Punk
podcast.body: Simple Plan was singled out in the mid-2000s as a band that was "too light" or "too poppy for punk." As a result, some alt-rock radio stations declined to feature their music, arguing that they attracted fans who were "too young" and not sufficiently aligned with authentic punk or alternative sensibilities. "groups like Headley and Simple Plan and Good Charlotte were maybe a little too light."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contemporary Powerpop
podcast.body: Simple Plan is mentioned as a current band that belongs to the Powerpop tradition. Their presence indicates that the genre continues to evolve and inspire new acts, maintaining a musical lineage that stretches back to 1963. "Well we have Jimmy Eat World, OkGo, All American Rejects, Simple Plan, maybe Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Decline in Popularity (2010s)
podcast.body: This band's popularity in the 2010s was significantly less than it had been previously, reflecting the general decline of the pop punk genre. "Some 41, simple plant and newfound glory were nowhere as big as they had once been."

podcast.title: Influenced by Blink-182
podcast.body: Simple Plan is identified as one of the bands that demonstrates the influence of Blink-182, suggesting that Blink-182's work has had a discernible effect on their music or career trajectory. "Some 41 good Charlotte simple-plan panic at the disco, followed boy, headly, billy talent, you would meet six, paramour, you know, you get the idea."

podcast.title: Legacy of Mid-90s Punk Revival
podcast.body: Simple Plan is one of the bands whose existence can be directly attributed to the impact of the mid-1990s punk rock revival. "It's certainly not a stretch to say the groups like Simple Plan... wouldn't have existed had it not been for what happened in the middle 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Third Wave Emo Chart Success
podcast.body: Simple Plan was among the bands whose emo records achieved mainstream success during the third wave of emo (early 2000s), with their albums reaching the top 10 on charts. "Emo records from bands like...Simple Plan... all rocketed into the top 10 on the album charts."

xref.title: Influence on Pop Punk
xref.body: Blink-182 is considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century. Their style and career trajectory have left a significant mark on numerous artists across the genre, inspiring bands like Sum 41, Good Charlotte, Simple Plan, Panic! At The Disco, Fall Out Boy, Hedley, Billy Talent, You Me At Six, and Paramore. "Blink has to be considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century."

xref.title: Pop Punk Heritage Act
xref.body: Blink-182 was identified as one of the "Big Heritage Acts" of Pop Punk that kept the spirit of the genre alive in the 2010s, despite its popularity being nowhere near its 90s or 2000s peaks. There was also a sentiment in some punk circles to reclaim punk from "Corporatized Punk" exemplified by bands like Blink-182. "The Big Heritage Acts were still there, you know, offspring, link quantity to some 41 simple plan, and they kept the spirit alive." "There's also the sense in some quarters that Punk needs to be torn down and rebuilt, reclaimed from the so-called Croppered Punk, exemplified by Blink-Wentety 2-Some41 in the offspring."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
